hook.line: If your TikTok views are low, she guarantees you are making one critical mistake.
hook.visual: Selfie-cam close-up in a parked car; white 'SEO FOR BEGINNERS' title box and red 'Part 1' tag at top, one bold white word at a time over her chest.

beats.what: Callout to viewers with low views plus a promised single mistake, first word at 0 s.
Long self-intro and credentials as a growth coach before any tip.
Asks for saves and shares, then comments and follows, before the content starts.
'Back into it': names the mistake, lack of SEO categorisation, and defines SEO.
First jump cut: TikTok framed as a search engine trying to climb the rankings.
Tip 1, the 'trifecta': on-screen text, first spoken words and hashtags all repeat the topic.
Small phone screen recording inset at top right shows typing in the TikTok text editor.
Tip 2 after a cut: write keywords in a text box and drag them off-screen so only the AI reads them.
Wrap-up: SEO is the first step to going viral.
Pitch for profile audits and one-on-one coaching via link in bio.

why_it_works: The opening addresses a specific pain (low views) and guarantees a single cause, so viewers who feel that pain stay to find out which mistake it is.
The 'drag keywords off-screen' trick is a concrete, copyable hack, which drives saves and shares (3,283 shares on 122k plays).
A fixed 'SEO FOR BEGINNERS / Part 1' title stays on screen the whole time, so a viewer joining mid-video knows the topic and that a series follows.
Asking for a comment with 'your biggest question' feeds the comment count (2,335 comments).
weaknesses: The first tip arrives only around 28 s; nearly 20 s go to self-intro and engagement asks.
One static car shot with 4 cuts in 102 s (2.35 cuts/min) and no punch-ins; nothing visual changes for the first 39 s.
The phone screen recording inset is tiny and sits beside the title, so the demo of the hack is hard to read.
The measure file puts 74% of text outside the safe area.
for_robert: Steal the persistent series title box at the top ('topic + Part 1') so every frame tells a scroller what the reel is about; avoid her 20-second intro and get to the first tip within 5 s.
